proposedQuiz.rationale: Three existing visual contrasts: 部 has right-hand 阝 instead of 刂; 倍 has left-hand 亻 and the same stacked right part; 副 keeps right-hand 刂 but has a different left block. Their current ordinary answer meanings do not describe dissecting/splitting open. This is not a claim that historical dictionaries give them no shared glosses; 字通's historical 副/剖 discussion is explicitly not adopted as modern identity or origin.

proposedTeachingConstraints: Use structure-unclassified and an explicitly labelled modern-shape mnemonic: 立-over-口 on the left, right-hand 刂 as positional 刀. Do not turn the SVG phon attribute or gaiji-incomplete 字通 discussion into historical proof.
Explain 剖 as dissect/split open in this teaching scope, not an all-purpose standalone replacement for 分ける.
解剖する takes the object を. Physical context concerns cutting open to examine internal structure; not only determining cause of death. No graphic/procedural medical lesson.

Use selective kana and English translations. Proposed illustrative sentence: 医学生は解剖で体の構造を学びます。 (いがくせいはかいぼうでからだのこうぞうをまなびます。) — Medical students learn the body's structure through dissection. Original illustration, not an attested quotation.
For figurative analysis use the actually attested dictionary phrase 事件を解剖する (じけんをかいぼうする), analyze a case, with attribution; do not manufacture a collocation to create a spelling distinction.
解剖学 かいぼうがく means anatomy; it is recognition-only here, not another required article or per-kanji metadata reading.
Keep full dictionary restrictions and primary readings separate. No frequency ranking from priority flags, no unsupported etymology, no inferred word level.
